answers.core: Well, it can't technically be an addon. Why this feature can essentially only be implemented in the source code (*without problems) and why it would be worth adding in principle, I described above.
answers.workaround:
Theoretically, you can do it like this:
- set the initial values ​​of the window under the boot splash
- disable the real boot splash
- set the fake boot splash as the first scene
- set the desired values ​​at the end of the real or not so real boot
However, there are two nuances:
- why bother so much?
- working with interface elements and especially 2D nodes will turn into hell if the game should not have a default resolution of 500x300, although this can be avoided by making a fake boot splash at the very end of work on the project (and then you will have to edit a huge number of aligns hehe)
